records.label: Think and Discuss
records.quote: In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent
records.text: In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent the set of X = {a, b, c, d, e} went to the school library to read some books which are represented by the set Y = [ science, literature, culture and history] student A read a book in science and a book in culture, student b read a book in histroy, student c read a literary book, pupil e read a book of the historical books, but student d didn't read any of these books.
records.notes: Intro paragraph with picture 'Reading for all' (decorative). Misprints in print: 'histroy', Y bracket '[' instead of '{'.

records.label: Think and Discuss
records.quote: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from X to Y.
records.text: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from X to Y.

records.label: Think and Discuss
records.quote: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow diagram.
records.text: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow diagram.

records.quote: Notice that: The expression " read" connects some of the elements
records.text: Notice that: The expression "read" connects some of the elements of the set X with the elements of set Y, and it determines a relation between X and Y which is denoted by the symbol R. This relation can be represented by an arrow diagram - as shown in the opposite figure, where we draw an arrow beginning from the student and ending at the type of books he reads.

records.quote: X Y a b c d e Science art culture history
records.caption: Arrow diagram from set X = a, b, c, d, e to set Y = Science, art, culture, history. Arrows: a→Science, a→culture, b→history, c→culture (appears; c's arrow crosses toward culture/science), e→history; d has no arrow. Y lists science, art, culture, history.
records.notes: Arrow endpoints read from small figure; verify (text says c read literary, figure has no literature element, and shows 'art').

records.quote: We can also express the relation from X to Y by the net
records.text: We can also express the relation from X to Y by the net of the following ordered pairs: {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, Histrory), (c, Literature), (e, History)}. This set of ordered pairs are called the relation R.

records.label: Think
records.quote: Is R a subset from the cartesian product X × Z?
records.text: Is R a subset from the cartesian product $X \times Z$?

misprints.notes: R is a relation from X to Y, so Z is likely a slip

records.quote: The relation from X to Y where X, Y are two non-empty sets
records.claim: A relation from X to Y, where X, Y are two non-empty sets, connects some or all of the elements of X with some or all of the elements of Y.

records.quote: X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection
records.claim: X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection in each ordered pair belongs to X and the second projection belongs to Y.

records.quote: If R is a relation from X to Y , then R ⊂ X × Y
records.claim: If R is a relation from X to Y, then R ⊂ X × Y.

records.quote: The relation from a set to itself
records.text: The relation from a set to itself

records.quote: If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself)
records.claim: If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself), then R is called a relation on X and R ⊂ X × X.

records.label: Example
records.quote: If X = {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} and R is a given relation on X
records.stem: If $X=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and R is a given relation on X where a R b means: «The number a is the additive inverse of the number b» for each of a, b ∈ X. Write the relation R and represent it by an arrow diagram and also by cartesian diagram.

records.caption: Arrow diagram of R on X: number line with points -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 joined by arcs (loop at 0, arcs between -1 and 1, and between -2 and 2), and an oval diagram of X with elements 0, -1, 1, -2, 2 with a loop at 0 and double arrows between -1 and 1, -2 and 2.

records.quote: Cartesian Diagram
records.caption: Cartesian diagram with both axes marked -2, -1, 0, 1, 2; points at (-2,2), (-1,1), (0,0), (1,-1), (2,-2).

objectives.label: Write a relation as ordered pairs
objectives.description: Express a relation from set X to set Y as a set of ordered pairs from a verbal statement.

objectives.label: Represent a relation by diagrams
objectives.description: Represent a relation from X to Y by an arrow diagram and by a cartesian diagram.

objectives.label: Relate a relation to the cartesian product
objectives.description: Recognize that a relation from X to Y connects elements of X with elements of Y and is a subset of X × Y.

objectives.label: Find and represent a relation on a set
objectives.description: Write and represent a relation from a set to itself (R ⊂ X × X) using arrow and cartesian diagrams.
